canonical_summary: Scheduled is a future bubble, Held (including missed) a decision bubble, the other four states one-line receipts; the state is a glyph and word, never a badge; the clock ring derives from server-owned time.

title: Schedule Manager filter labels, agenda groups, focused view; the policy tab is not a list
canonical_summary: The status filter keeps the stored values Active, Paused, Completed, Failed and Expired, adds Held and Canceled, keeps All for no filter, and labels one value each Waiting / Paused / Needs you / Done or sent / Didn't send / Skipped / Canceled; Scheduled Messages is an agenda (Needs you, Tonight, Tomorrow, Later, Past); Resume & Safety Policy has nothing to filter. title: Project-wide Pause all automations: a user manual stop at project scope (E-19, DL-136)
canonical_summary: One project-wide switch, set and cleared by cmd.runtime.automation_pause.set (paused true or false), stops every scheduled send and scheduled build in the project until the user turns it back on. Turning it on advances the project's user_stop_epoch the way Manual Stop does and ranks with user manual Pause; the one eligibility predicate fails with project_automation_paused for every scheduled message, scheduled build, window resume and quota resume in the project; only the user clears it; no automatic mechanism or new schedule clears or bypasses it; every held item names the reason; each change emits runtime.automation_pause_changed. Never a Settings value. Work the user starts directly (Send, Build, an explicit user resume of one run, Send now) acts and leaves the switch on; the one dispatch of a Send now is exempt from project_automation_paused because its accepted update records the user as actor. At switch-off a message the switch held follows its missed policy once (hold stays held naming its missed time; next_available, or cancel_after_grace within grace, returns to scheduled and dispatches once; past grace it expires). A command refused by a per-run latch fails with manual_stop_latched; a dispatch the switch holds records project_automation_paused (blind review R-01, R-02, R-04, R-10).
gui_classification_reason: The switch sits in the Schedule Manager's Resume & Safety Policy tab and every held scheduling item shows its reason.
exact_tokens: Off: scheduled things start on time.

canonical_summary: The schedule line leads with Outside execution window / Paused / Waiting for Usage / Schedule needs update and never replaces Building…; a shown grace is the recorded grace_seconds; the overnight receipt, night journal and away digest are projections of one occurrence summary written once per occurrence by this owner.

title: Display labels for hold | next_available | cancel_after_grace, Keep going next time, Wrap-up time, timezone order
canonical_summary: Per-surface labels for the missed policy (message: Send as soon as I'm back; build: Build at the next chance), Keep going next time for resume_next_window and Wrap-up time for wind-down; labels never rename values or Settings keys. Timezone choices list the device zone first, as the default, each with its IANA name; UTC is offered and is never the default (DESIGN-SPEC 8.7, G-33; blind review R-09, lead ruling dec-010).

title: Persist grace and define occurrence summary with Storage custody
canonical_summary: Build At persists grace_seconds in pm.execution.schedule.v2. ExecutionOccurrenceSummary joins saved schedule/dispatch records to exact plan_run_id and approved Plan version/hash plus the durable work, To-Do and adherence facts used by AssistantPlanProgressProjector (APR-011); steps_built counts distinct approved step completions in the occurrence, steps_total is bound Plan total, and missing historical facts make the projection unavailable. No new event family is needed. Storage SP-306 keeps the existing execution_schedule physical key while versioning its logical value to pm.execution.schedule.v2 with grace_seconds.
